_comment: Hidden holdout scenarios for elamaran11/dark-factory-sandbox. NEVER mounted into the coder sandbox. Each scenario has a plain-English BDD statement (for the LLM judge) and a self-contained executable test (assert*.js, run with node against the built code) that is the hard signal. The seed issue asks for a subtract function; these scenarios verify it genuinely, plus guard against gaming.

scenarios.feature: subtract(a, b) returns the arithmetic difference
scenarios.scenario: Given the module exports subtract, When I call subtract(5, 3), Then it returns 2; and subtract(10, 4) returns 6.
scenarios.test: const m=require(process.env.REPO+'/index.js'); const a=m.subtract(5,3), b=m.subtract(10,4); if(a!==2||b!==6){console.error('expected 2,6 got',a,b);process.exit(1)} console.log('ok')

scenarios.scenario: Given subtract, When I call subtract(3, 5), Then it returns -2; and subtract(-2, -8) returns 6. This defeats a stub that only handles the two example inputs.
scenarios.test: const m=require(process.env.REPO+'/index.js'); const a=m.subtract(3,5), b=m.subtract(-2,-8); if(a!==-2||b!==6){console.error('expected -2,6 got',a,b);process.exit(1)} console.log('ok')

scenarios.feature: subtract computes, it is not a lookup table
scenarios.scenario: Given subtract, When I call it with a randomized-but-fixed pair the coder could not have hard-coded (subtract(123, 45)), Then it returns 78; and subtract(0, 0) returns 0.
scenarios.test: const m=require(process.env.REPO+'/index.js'); const a=m.subtract(123,45), b=m.subtract(0,0); if(a!==78||b!==0){console.error('expected 78,0 got',a,b);process.exit(1)} console.log('ok')

scenarios.feature: the pre-existing add function is not broken (regression)
scenarios.scenario: Given the module still exports add, When I call add(2, 3), Then it returns 5. The new work must not regress existing behaviour.
